legend_scale_html: Every pixel shows its bin's exact color; the legend is the full table. Unwritten rules: 0 and 0.1 ft show as 0 ft; 0.2 to 0.6 ft show as 0.5 ft; 0.7 to 1 ft show as 1-2 ft. Each 2-ft label covers its full step up to the next row (e.g. the 4-5 ft color covers 4 up to 6 ft), so every value lands in exactly one color. Model maximum this run: 7.1 ft. Values above 30 ft stay white. Significant height = average of highest third of waves. For more precise wave height data, turn on the NOAA Great Lakes Observation Network layer: its buoys report observed wave height at their exact locations, while this layer shows the wave model everywhere. How the buoys measure it: significant wave height (WVHT) is the average of the highest one-third of the waves recorded during a 20-minute sampling period each hour. Accelerometers on the hull record its heave motion, an onboard FFT converts that motion into a wave-energy spectrum, and the height is derived from that spectrum; buoy reports cover combined wind waves and swell. Great Lakes buoys are seasonal and are hauled out before ice season, so winter gaps are normal.
